title: AI drafts before the board
intro: This round is about what the AI drafts before the board: the Case File summary, specialty briefs, Ask the Case File, review marks, the NCG export and voice. How they are used in the meeting comes in Round 12.

questions.question: Should the Case File summary compile by itself once the check is met?

options.label: Yes, by itself (Recommended)
options.description: The summary (24 to 34 s) compiles in the background the moment the check is met, so the doctor opens a ready draft.

options.label: When the owner marks ready
options.description: Compiled at the ready mark, so it uses the latest records; the owner sees it only after marking.

options.label: Doctor presses Compile
options.description: As today: nothing runs until someone asks.

questions.why: V2 4.4: the summary compiles only once every check is met; today a person presses Compile (J1). UX_notes.md point 3: give some initial analysis first without asking anything. K02: slow AI steps need progress feedback.
questions.notes: Order is: check met, then ready mark, then the summary compiles. R10-Q06 must not require a reviewed summary before ready (adapt its options).

questions.topic: Draft before the check is met
questions.question: Should a summary draft be allowed before the check is met?

options.label: Yes, marked incomplete (Recommended)
options.description: Like today's 'Compile draft anyway': every page names the missing records, and it cannot be exported or used to mark ready.

options.label: No, only after the check
options.description: The summary stays locked until the check is met; urgent cases wait or waive.

questions.why: The 'Compile draft anyway (marked incomplete)' button and summary.build(force) exist today (tb.js, routes). Cancer of Unknown Primary work-ups are often incomplete by nature (W4, T09).

questions.question: When records change after the summary was reviewed, what should happen?

options.label: New draft, reviewed one kept (Recommended)
options.description: A fresh draft compiles in the background; the reviewed version stays visible, marked 'changed since review', until a doctor reviews the new one.

options.label: Banner only, as today
options.description: A stale banner with Regenerate; the doctor decides when.

options.label: Replace and clear review
options.description: The new draft replaces the old at once and the review mark is removed.

questions.why: V1 4.5 Case File signature: the summary and briefs go stale when documents, confirmations, setting or level change; Regenerate is manual; the NCG export is refused while stale.

questions.question: Who may mark the Case File summary reviewed?

options.label: The owning consultant (Recommended)
options.description: Only the treating doctor who owns the Case File; their name goes on the print and the NCG export.

options.label: Any owning-department consultant
options.description: Any consultant of the owning department; quicker when the owner is away.

options.label: No mark, always AI draft
options.description: The summary is never marked reviewed; it is labelled an AI draft wherever it appears.

questions.why: Today any placed reader may mark an AI draft reviewed or flag it for correction (G09, matrix 'review'); the export footer says 'reviewed by X' or 'AI draft, awaiting expert review'. Settled: 'expert over the loop'; R01 defines who approves what.

questions.question: What may a resident, PG or fellow do with the summary?

options.label: Prepare; consultant approves (Recommended)
options.description: The resident compiles, adds notes and removes sentences; it shows 'prepared by Dr R, awaiting Dr C' until the consultant marks it reviewed.

options.label: Compile only
options.description: The resident may start the compile and read it, but not change it.

options.label: Read only
options.description: The resident sees the summary; the consultant does everything.

questions.why: I03 liked (resident prepares drafts, consultant approves, both names in the audit). Research: in India residents usually prepare the case summary and slides (widely assumed, not found in published sources); US residents carried 39% to 72% of preparation hours. R03 sets resident rights in general.

questions.question: How may doctors change the summary text?

options.label: Notes added, AI text locked (Recommended)
options.description: Doctors remove sentences and add their own notes, labelled with their name; AI sentences cannot be reworded, so each keeps its verified quote.

options.label: Edit any sentence, labelled
options.description: Any sentence may be reworded; edited ones show 'edited by Dr X' and link to the original quote.

options.label: No edits, flag and regenerate
options.description: The only fix is 'flag for correction' and compiling again.

questions.why: Lajmi 2026: an editable LLM summary took 6:55 vs 8:47 min manual; Hartmann 2026: summaries rewritten 3.5 times. Invariant: every value shown as fact carries a verified verbatim quote, so a reworded sentence becomes the doctor's statement, not a verified one.

questions.question: What should doctors see of the items the AI wrote but verification removed?

options.label: A count, list on tap (Recommended)
options.description: '3 items removed: could not be verified' opens the list with each reason; never in the print, the export or the room screen.

options.label: Audit only
options.description: Removed items are hidden from screens and kept in the audit for the Vaidyx team.

options.label: Shown struck through
options.description: Removed items stay in place, crossed out, with the reason beside them.

questions.why: V1 6.4: the summary, briefs and answers keep removed items with the reason (quote not found, number not in the source, scope guardrail); reviewers open 'N removed items (failed verification, not facts)'. AI role need (data.js): see quickly which statements are verified and which were removed.
questions.answer: A count, or a short summary of what was removed
questions.own_words: A count is enough, or a summary of what was deleted, so that it becomes an active learning opportunity for Vaidyx: a good opportunity for us in the backend.
questions.notes: Removed items are also stored for the team's quality review and prompt / rule improvement (active learning). Real patient data used only under the hospital's data rules (round 15).

questions.question: Should items whose quote matches the record only approximately be shown at all?

options.label: No, exact quotes only (Recommended)
options.description: As today: an item is shown only when its quote is found word for word; others are removed.

options.label: Yes, flagged 'check source'
options.description: Shown with a warning and left out of print and export until a doctor reviews; more content, more checking.

questions.why: V1 6.5 near-match (TB_NEAR_MATCH) is built and off by default 'until the clinical team accepts it': same numbers and negation words required, small spelling or spacing differences allowed. Project rule: no lossy layer.

questions.question: When should the specialty briefs be prepared?

options.label: Before, for all four heads (Recommended)
options.description: Radiology, Pathology, Medical and Surgical Oncology briefs (13 to 17 s each) are ready with the summary, readable before the meeting; absent heads' agents reuse them.

options.label: At session start, absent only
options.description: As today: only the agent of a head not recorded present prepares, when the coordinator starts the session.

options.label: On request only
options.description: A doctor presses Prepare on the Specialty support tab when wanted.

questions.why: D2: briefs run at session start for heads not recorded present; a current brief (same signature) is reused; the Specialty support tab can prepare one any time. One shared H200: four briefs add about a minute of reasoner time per Case File. R12 decides how agents speak in the meeting.
questions.answer: With the summary, all five heads (Recommended)
questions.notes: Prepared when the owner marks ready (with the summary, R09-Q01); five heads incl. Radiation Oncology (R02-Q04).

questions.question: Who may mark a specialty brief reviewed?

options.label: A doctor of that specialty (Recommended)
options.description: The Radiology brief only by a Radiology doctor, and so on; until then it shows 'AI draft' in the meeting.

options.label: The owning consultant
options.description: The treating doctor reviews every brief of the Case File.

options.label: Nobody, always AI draft
options.description: Briefs are never marked reviewed; the board treats them as role-specific AI support.

questions.why: G09: any placed reader can mark any AI draft reviewed, not tied to the specialty. The agent log uses 'reviewed' to decide what prints. R01 defines 'expert over the loop'; R08-Q10 may let the specialist do this with the confirmation.

questions.question: Should useful answers from Ask the Case File be kept on the Case File?

options.label: Doctor pins chosen answers (Recommended)
options.description: A doctor pins a cited answer; it shows under 'Notes' in the summary and in the room; unpinned answers are not kept (the audit keeps the question).

options.label: Keep every answer
options.description: A history of all questions and cited answers on the Case File, visible to its team.

options.label: Not kept, as today
options.description: Ask again when needed.

questions.why: Stage 6: cited statements, 'not documented' or a scope refusal, median 6 s; the audit stores the question. Residents prepare the board pack (I03), so answers found before the meeting can save time in it (R12).

questions.question: Where should voice input for questions be offered first?

options.label: Every question box (Recommended)
options.description: Push-to-talk on Ask the Case File and each agent box; the words appear for editing before Ask; the audio is discarded after transcription.

options.label: Board room only
options.description: Voice only in the meeting, where typing is hardest.

options.label: Not yet
options.description: Text only until the new interface is built.

questions.why: audio_feature.md: research complete 15 Oct, waiting for 'proceed'; Whisper large-v3-turbo on our GPU (2.3 GB, about 0.1 to 0.2 s per utterance), English first, audio not stored, the microphone needs HTTPS or localhost. Voice only fills text boxes, never runs a command. Settled: board members' end-of-meeting pop-up has voice (R13).
questions.notes: No voice in question boxes for now. The settled end-of-meeting pop-up keeps its voice option (text and voice).

questions.question: What may Vaidyx read aloud when a doctor asks?

options.label: Verified answers (Recommended)
options.description: Ask the Case File and agent answers, statement by statement, with their sources named.

options.label: Case File summary
options.description: The whole summary or one section, for a doctor away from the screen.

options.label: Points for review
options.description: Only the items flagged for a clinician to look at.

options.label: Specialty briefs
options.description: An absent head's brief read out, for example in the room.

questions.why: audio_feature.md: Kokoro-82M reads only text already on screen (first audio under 100 ms on the GPU); units, TNM strings and drug names need a clinical text normaliser first (section 5a). Read-out adds nothing that is not shown.
questions.own_words: Don't talk about voice now; work only with text for the initial build of the new interface. After I confirm it over several iterations, I will talk about speech and giving Vaidyx ears and a mouth.

questions.question: When may the NCG Virtual Tumour Board slides (.pptx) be exported?

options.label: Only after review (Recommended)
options.description: Export needs the summary marked reviewed; the footer names the reviewer.

options.label: Any current summary, as today
options.description: Allowed while it is an AI draft; the footer says 'AI draft, awaiting expert review'.

options.label: Reviewed and de-identified by default
options.description: Needs review, and removes name, UHID and date of birth unless the doctor turns that off, for hub and spoke referral (I18).

questions.why: V1 4.6: fills NCG's own 6-slide case template from the verified summary, every sentence cited; refused while missing, stale or flagged for correction, allowed as an AI draft. I18 (de-identified export) proposed; the NCG VTB template asks for de-identified clinical details.

questions.question: Earlier (R09-Q01) the summary is written only when the doctor marks ready, but the new Case File page IS the summary. When should its lines appear?

options.label: Lines live now, AI text at ready (Recommended)
options.description: From the first fetch each line is filled straight from verified report quotes (no AI writing), blanks show gaps; AI-written parts (history paragraph, specialty briefs) come at the ready mark.

options.label: Everything live from the start
options.description: AI writes all text from the first fetch and rewrites on change.

options.label: Page shows only gaps until ready
options.description: Summary appears at the ready mark.

questions.why: Added in the final answer check (17 Oct): resolves a conflict or gap found by the check.
questions.answer: Lines live now, AI text at ready (Recommended)
questions.notes: Supersedes R09-Q01 / Q02 for the fill-in summary: slot lines from verified facts are live; AI prose and briefs at the ready mark.

questions.question: Which specialty briefs should be prepared in advance at the ready mark?

options.label: 5 heads at ready, Nuclear Med on click (Recommended)
options.description: Radiology, Pathology, Medical, Surgical, Radiation Oncology at the ready mark; Nuclear Medicine when its card is opened.

options.label: All 6 at ready
options.description: More GPU time.

options.label: None in advance
options.description: Each on click.

questions.why: Added in the final answer check (17 Oct): resolves a conflict or gap found by the check.
questions.answer: 5 heads at ready, Nuclear Med on click (Recommended)
